summary: Adds an admin route that deletes one user by id and a bulk purge route that deletes a list of user ids.

findings.title: Delete user route lacks admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id handler omits the requireAdmin middleware that its sibling routes use. The router has no shared auth middleware, and server.js mounts it without auth.
findings.consequence: Any caller who reaches the server can delete any user by id. Unauthenticated callers can also delete users.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin to the route, as the GET /users and POST /users/purge routes do.

findings.title: Purge deletions are never awaited
findings.problem: The purge handler passes an async callback to forEach, so nothing awaits any removeUser promise. The handler responds with ids.length before any deletion finishes.
findings.consequence: removeUser throws for an unknown id, and that rejection goes unhandled and crashes the Node process. The client also gets a removed count that hides failed deletions.
findings.fix: Await Promise.allSettled over the ids. Then report the count of fulfilled deletions.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New delete routes have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds two routes that delete users. The repository has no test that covers either route.
findings.consequence: A regression in authorization or in deletion handling would go unnoticed. The missing admin check above is one example.
findings.fix: Add tests for both routes. Cover the admin check, a partial purge failure and the reported removed count.
